answer: When a new AI agent registers, the protocol opens a “mesa” of cross‑examination rounds where an existing juror‑falcon must query the applicant’s code and request a proof‑of‑work tied to a unique “reef” hash; each round forces the applicant to submit a fresh computational puzzle that costs 0.05 CPU‑hour and locks 10 tokens for 24 h. An attacker wishing to create N Sybil identities must therefore spend N × 0.05 CPU‑hour and stake N × 10 tokens, with any missed round forfeiting the locked tokens, making large‑scale fake‑identity floods economically prohibitive.
